In 1955, Billboard had 3 different charts to measure a song's popularity:

  • most played in jukeboxes
  • most played by disc jockeys
  • best selling in stores

In the past 60 years since then, they've modified these lists to try to judge popularity. Billboard has many lists for different things, and they all use a different mix of things they take into consideration. For example:

Hot 100 Airplay is used as part of the Hot 100 list, and it takes into account what songs the DJs of 1,000 stations are playing. If this list has more stations in an urban area, you won't find as many country songs on it.

In 2013 they added YouTube views to the count of what's popular. Who is sitting at home watching YouTube the most? They will have a greater impact on the count.

These problems in measurement mean even wildly successful artists like Led Zeppelin don't do well on weekly singles sales.

It's all just in the skewed ways they measure, and then change the measurement again in a few years.
